openings.claim: Preserve confusion counting and the item selection log, but break the table-to-selection feedback interface. A fixed inspection itinerary may produce a reproducible bounded decision without adaptive aggregate feedback.
openings.delta: Freeze an itinerary before constructing the confusion table: prioritize flagged rows where baseline and candidate predictions differ, cycle across their slices, and break ties by supplied record identifier. The log associates each attempted identifier with this criterion, its result or withheld status, and allowance consumed. Confusion tables still group paired predictions and available labels into count cells; their outputs cannot reorder or supplement the itinerary. Direct adjudication results feed counting and logging separately. Do not restore table-to-selection feedback.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, which adaptively selects from current confusion-table deficits while keeping the same log, the fixed itinerary will sometimes yield different inspected identifiers and different advance/reject/unresolved reports. Whether it improves decision support is unknown. It fails its proposed advantage if the rival produces more supported, key-consistent decisions within equal resources.
openings.probe: Use the two matched copies and independently reset sixteen-row allowances. Predetermine four withheld flagged rows and apply identical withholding to both workflows; log unsuccessful attempts without charging allowance. For each workflow, freeze its report within seventy minutes. Compute total and slice improvement intervals: resolved supplied labels contribute exact paired correctness differences; unresolved flagged rows contribute zero when predictions agree and [-1,1] otherwise. Advance only when the total lower bound is at least four and every slice lower bound is at least -2; reject only when the total upper bound is below four or some slice upper bound is below -2; otherwise unresolved. Open the full-label key only after both reports freeze. Compare key consistency, supported decisions, inspected identifiers, affected slices, adjudications and time. Wide intervals after sixteen adjudications or excessive computation defeat practical usefulness; the cap alone establishes neither feasibility nor information gain.
assumptions: Unflagged supplied labels are accepted as given for this task.
Itinerary construction, counting and interval computation fit the supplied environment and seventy minutes; unverified.

assessment: A workflow probe, not deployment evidence. Both parent functions remain; only aggregate feedback into inspection selection is removed. Report uncertainty whenever available adjudications cannot certify the unchanged rule.
